summary: Enhance your risk management skills with our IFRS training course. Learn to navigate financial standards effectively and boost your career potential today.
lede: IFRS-based risk management connects financial reporting choices with credit, market, and liquidity risk decisions. For risk, finance, audit, treasury, and portfolio professionals, the course develops practical ways to interpret expected credit loss assumptions, assess fair value and liquidity exposures, and turn IFRS disclosures and scenario results into clear information for decision makers.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who regularly engage with risk, IFRS-based reports, and financial decisions. It is tailored for those who need to interpret, challenge, and apply IFRS requirements in their roles.
audience: Risk managers and risk officers in banks
Credit managers and portfolio managers using ECL
Public sector and SOE finance teams
modules: IFRS and the Risk Management Mindset
Financial Instruments, Classification and Risk Exposure
Expected Credit Loss (ECL) and Credit Risk under IFRS 9
Fair Value, Valuation Uncertainty, and Market Risk (IFRS 13)
Liquidity, Funding and Off-Balance Sheet Risk in IFRS Reports
Risk Disclosures, Sensitivity Analysis and Narrative Reporting
IFRS, Capital Adequacy and Regulatory Alignment
Governance, Judgement and Model Risk in IFRS-based Risk Numbers
Scenario Analysis, Stress Testing and IFRS
Communicating IFRS-based Risk Insights to Decision Makers
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of financial reporting and risk management principles. Prior experience with IFRS would be beneficial but not required.
